auth-state.mechanism: META_API_KEY presence + provider list in ~/.config/muse/auth.json (credential type and account identity are not exposed by muse)

account-enumeration.mechanism: muse has no whoami/accounts command; CCSwap-registered only

registration.mechanism: Browser: the login file is kept only when it holds a token. API key: accepted only when it is providers.meta.api_key of a registered browser login, and linked to that login by alias

switch.mechanism: Browser logins: ccswap keeps a login only when the file holds a token, swaps Muse's auth.json, and accepts the switch when `muse usage` does not say not logged in. A keychain pointer is refused. API-key accounts are for `ccswap muse run` and are not menu switches

usage.mechanism: `muse usage --json` (no model turn): tier, 5-hour and weekly used % with reset times. Each browser login is measured from its own stored auth.json under a private XDG_CONFIG_HOME with TBH_CREDENTIAL_BACKEND=file. An API key reports the linked login's allowance. The signed-in login is read in place

auto-switch.mechanism: `ccswap muse auto` or the menu bar toggle: when the signed-in login reaches a gate (autoswitch.threshold, threshold5h, threshold7d) ccswap switches to the browser login with the most room. Running Muse sessions keep the previous login until restarted

session-isolation.mechanism: Every muse child gets TBH_CREDENTIAL_BACKEND=file. A login that is not the signed-in one is measured under a private XDG_CONFIG_HOME. `ccswap muse run` still passes META_API_KEY for an API-key account

auth-state.mechanism: this version has no JSON listing; providers are read (names/types only) from the legacy auth.json, one credential per provider

account-enumeration.mechanism: this version has no JSON listing; providers are read (names/types only) from the legacy auth.json, one credential per provider

registration.mechanism: alias for a provider/account OpenCode already lists

switch.mechanism: this OpenCode has no `auth switch` (added in newer releases); use `opencode auth login` or the TUI /connect

usage.mechanism: local statistics per provider and model (tokens, OpenCode's USD cost estimate; 24h/7d/30d/all) via a read-only `opencode db` aggregate, or `opencode stats` text on older releases. Provider quotas and per-account usage: not reported

auto-switch.mechanism: no verified per-account quota to compare

session-isolation.mechanism: credentials are resolved by the shared OpenCode server, not per process

detect.mechanism: PATH lookup for `kiro-cli` (not the IDE launcher `kiro`)

account-enumeration.mechanism: only the single active login is visible (`whoami`); no account list

registration.mechanism: login: identity metadata from `whoami` (no tokens copied); api-key: stdin/prompt into CCSwap's 0600 store

switch.mechanism: login accounts: confirmed `kiro-cli logout` + `kiro-cli login <flags>` (interactive), verified with `whoami`. API-key accounts: not switchable (process-scoped) -- use `ccswap kiro run`

usage.mechanism: `/usage` is interactive-only; no documented machine-readable interface

auto-switch.mechanism: switching a login needs an interactive logout/login

session-isolation.mechanism: API-key accounts: child gets KIRO_API_KEY (headless). Login accounts share the one machine-wide login and cannot run side by side

logout.mechanism: `kiro-cli logout`, only inside an explicit login switch
